metadata.summary: Background: The molecular mechanisms underlying heart failure (HF) following myocardial infarction (MI) (HF-MI) remain incompletely understood, and whole-transcriptome profiling studies hold significant promise for disease prevention and treatment. Methods: Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed on post-MI patients with and without HF to analyze differentially expressed mRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs, along with functional enrichment analysis. Co-expression networks linking lncRNA-mRNA and circRNA-mRNA pairs, as well as ceRNA networks involving lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA and circRNA-miRNA-mRNA interactions, were constructed for differentially expressed (DE) RNAs. Key lncRNAs were validated by RT-qPCR. Transcriptional factor-lncRNA networks were constructed, and key relationships were verified using RIP-PCR. Results: Patients with HF-MI exhibited marked elevation of NT-proBNP and significant reduction in LVEF%. Transcriptome-wide analysis revealed 228 DE-mRNAs, 700 DE-lncRNAs, and 1188 DE-circRNAs in HF-MI compared to non-heart failure patients (NHF-MI). Construction of the ceRNA network identified hsa-miR-6089 and hsa-miR-6771-5p as key miRNAs in the lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA network, while hsa-miR-1207-5p and hsa-miR-10392-3p were key miRNAs in the circRNA-miRNA-mRNA network. PVT1, SNHG5, TTN-AS1, HCP5, and OIP5-AS1 were identified as the five key DE-lncRNAs, with PVT1/SNHG5 showing upregulation and TTN-AS1/HCP5/OIP5-AS1 exhibiting downregulation. The transcription factor-lncRNA network primarily involves GLIS3-HCP5 and ZNF135-PVT1, with validated associative interactions. Conclusion: This study systematically mapped the regulatory network of HF-MI, revealing the roles of the GLIS3-HCP5 and ZNF135-PVT1 regulatory axes in HF-MI, thereby providing a basis for exploring novel therapeutic strategies.

observations.text: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by abnormal cortical activity, which can be captured using electroencephalography (EEG). Although machine learning (ML) has shown promise for diagnosing several neurological conditions, comprehensive evaluation of classical ML and deep learning (DL) methods, together with physiologically meaningful explanations, remains limited for RTT. This study analyses resting-state, eyes-closed EEG recordings from RTT patients and healthy controls using both power spectral density (PSD)-based ML and end-to-end DL frameworks. Classical ML models, including Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were trained on PSD features, while EEG-specific DL architectures, including ShallowConvNet, DeepConvNet, EEGNet, and EEG Conformer, were trained directly on preprocessed EEG signals. Subjectwise cross-validation was used to avoid data leakage, with balanced accuracy as the primary performance metric because it equally accounts for sensitivity and specificity. Random Forest achieved the best performance among the classical ML models, whereas EEGNet achieved the highest DL performance. An ablation study indicated that 4-second EEG epochs offered the optimal trade-off between model performance and robustness. Model interpretability was investigated using SHAP for Random Forest and occlusion sensitivity analysis for EEGNet. Both methods consistently identified delta and theta oscillations, along with centro-frontal brain regions, as key contributors to RTT classification. These findings show that both PSD-based machine learning and end-to-end deep learning methods can reliably identify RTT and highlight common neurophysiological biomarkers, offering an interpretable framework for EEG-based diagnosis and biomarker discovery for Rett Syndrome.
observations.title: EEG Biomarkers for Rett Syndrome: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning with Explainable AI

metadata.summary: Background: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) followed by a reperfusion results in a phasic response by cardiac macrophages. During the first 7 days after AMI, macrophage populations exhibit dynamic phenotypic changes. Ultimately, inflammatory damage results in ventricular remodeling and fibrosis. Macrophages are critical to cardiac function and long-term prognoses. Objective: Elucidate the spatiotemporal behavior of specific macrophage subtypes during  AMI and identify novel genes with prospective therapeutic potential. Methods: We implement an IRI mouse model of AMI to assess cardiac macrophage behavior during AMI. RCM were isolated using flow cytometry and analyzed with NanoString. Pathway enrichment analysis annotated statistically significant genes. We employed transcriptome-wide, spatiotemporal analysis of cardiac tissue samples during  AMI.

ObjectiveQuantifying physiological dynamics from nonstationary time series for clinical decision-making is challenging, especially when comparing data across different subjects. We propose a solution, called Universal Coordinate (UC), and validate it using two real-world surgical databases, focusing on underutilized arterial blood pressure (ABP) signals.

MethodWe apply a manifold learning algorithm, Dynamic Diffusion Maps (DDMap) under the novel UC, to quantify dynamics from nonstationary time series so that cross-subject comparison can be achieved. The method is demonstrated using ABP signal and validated with liver transplant and cardiovascular surgery databases, both containing clinical outcomes. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess robustness and identify optimal parameters.

ResultsThe UC solution is validated by significant correlations between the derived index and clinical outcomes. Sensitivity analyses confirm the algorithms stability and help optimize parameters.

ConclusionsUC enables across-subject comparison of ABP signals dynamics quantified by DDMap, and hence repurposes typically discarded ABP signals in the operating room and can be applied to other nonstationary biomedical signals in both hospital and homecare settings.

observations.text: Periodontitis is an archetypical mucosal inflammatory disease in which microbiome dysbiosis at the tooth-epithelial interface interacts with host genetic and behavioral risk factors to drive immune-mediated tissue destruction. Although subgingival microbiome compositional shifts are thought to parallel disease severity, microbiome variation at the population-level and its relationship to periodontal clinical phenotypes and disease-modifying factors remain poorly defined. Here, we use unsupervised manifold learning to map the compositional landscape of the subgingival microbiome in 1,355 adults spanning periodontal health to severe periodontitis. We identified eight latent microbiome states organized along a branching continuum from eubiosis to dysbiosis. An intermediate microbial configuration marked ecological destabilization and bifurcation into two distinct periodontitis-associated dysbiotic trajectories, distinguished by links to gingival inflammation and smoking. Although the microbiome trajectories broadly tracked periodontal destruction, a minority of individuals showed discordant microbiome-clinical phenotypes, with some individuals with periodontitis retaining otherwise eubiotic microbiomes enriched for low-abundance pathobionts, while some cases of health or mild disease had highly dysbiotic communities, suggesting distinct host susceptibility. Together, these findings define a population-scale ecological landscape of the subgingival microbiome, reveal divergent trajectories to periodontal dysbiosis, and highlight heterogeneity in the relationship between microbial community structure and clinical disease expression.
observations.title: A population-scale landscape of the subgingival microbiome reveals divergent routes to periodontal dysbiosis

observations.text: Analysing cardiac motion from label free imaging can be difficult, especially when recordings vary in quality or show complex movement. We developed a Python-based pipeline that automatically measures beat rate, contraction, speed from transmitted light timelapse data. The workflow runs in a Jupyter notebook and uses straightforward steps that can be followed easily, making the analysis accessible including to users with limited coding experience. Using human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes imaged on a Zeiss Cell Discoverer 7, the pipeline produced beat rates, contraction and contraction speed measurements that matched expected behaviour. To test wider use, we applied the same workflow to killifish larvae heart recordings and public datasets, changing only basic input parameters. The pipeline performed consistently across these different systems and did not require changes to the underlying code. By supporting clear parameter control and use across laboratories, microscopy platforms and repositories, this approach strengthens reproducible analysis of cardiac motion from label free imaging.

observations.text:
Histopathological growth patterns, predominantly the presence of an encapsulated rim, serve as powerful prognostic biomarkers in colorectal liver metastases. However, conventional visual estimation is limited by interobserver variability, human rounding bias, and categorical thresholds. We aimed to develop and externally validate a deep-learning segmentation framework that produces continuous, spatially resolved, and objective encapsulation metrics from routine whole-slide images.

In this multicenter study of chemo-naive resected CRLM patients, a modified nnU-Net architecture was developed on 40 pixel-annotated H&E-stained WSIs to segment liver parenchyma, tumor, and the encapsulation interface. Model performance was optimized across spatial resolutions. An automated continuous AI encapsulation score was computed to determine patient-level metrics. The prognostic value for 5-year overall survival was evaluated using restricted cubic spline Cox regression, a log-rank optimized threshold, and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses across a main cohort (Erasmus MC; n = 546, 1,910 WSIs) and an independent external validation cohort (Radboud UMC; n = 212, 615 WSIs).

The segmentation network achieved optimal tissue boundary delineation at a resolution of 2.0 {micro}m/pixel on the 40 annotated slides (overall foreground DICE: 0.86 {+/-} 0.09; encapsulation DICE: 0.70 {+/-} 0.11). Spline modeling demonstrated that while visual assessment displayed non-linear hazard plateaus, the continuous AI encapsulation score exhibited a linear reduction in mortality risk across the critical intermediate range (25%-75% encapsulation, p = 7.81 x 10-4). Log-rank optimization identified a primary global threshold at 47.4% (p = 3.73 x 10-8), which in confirmed significant OS stratification in external validation (p = 0.018). A secondary threshold was found at 69% (p = 2.93 x 10-6) that captured high-encapsulation favorable-risk patients matching the current manual 100% Rotterdam cut-off.

Our deep-learning model transforms qualitative HGP grading into a continuous, explainable, and fully automated prognostic biometry. By eliminating observer subjectivity and capturing fine-grained risk gradients, the model establishes a scalable, standardized foundation for CRLM risk stratification on digital pathology.
observations.title: AI-Enhanced Segmentation and Scoring of Histopathological Growth Patterns in Resected Colorectal Liver Metastases

observations.text: The potential role of the cerebellum in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia has received relatively insufficient attention. Prior studies characterized cerebellar abnormalities mainly at the group level, without fully considering the heterogeneity of the disease. Here, we applied a machine learning approach (Subtype and Stage Inference, SuStaIn) to cross-sectional 3D volumetric MRIs of the cerebellum, including a total of 3,550 individuals with schizophrenia (1423 females; mean age: 32.3 {+/-} 12.0 years) and 5,771 healthy controls (HC) (2,861 females; mean age: 32.5 {+/-} 12.9 years), from 34 sites worldwide. SuStaIn identified three distinct spatiotemporal trajectories in cerebellar gray matter volume reduction, respectively originating in lobule X (subtype 1), lobule III (subtype 2) and lobule VIIb (subtype 3), with subtypes 1 and 3 corresponding to the posterior lobe and subtype 2 to the anterior lobe. These trajectories were cross-sectionally inferred in 1,588 individuals with schizophrenia and replicated in another independent samples of 1,334 and 628 patients, respectively. Multimodal analyses using neuroimaging, transcriptomic and behavioral data revealed subtype-specific biological characteristics in brain morphological patterns, cerebellar-cortical connectivity, gene expression and clinical symptoms. Specifically, subtype-related genes were enriched in metabolism-related processes and immunity-related processes, respectively, in subtype 1 and subtype 2; subtype 3 showed more severe brain abnormalities and worse cognitive symptoms. Treatment data from 381 patients, with up to 12 months of follow-up, revealed poorer response to antipsychotic medications in subtype 2 and subtype 3, but better response to transcranial magnetic stimulation in subtype 1, which also had worse emotion-related symptoms. Together, our findings offer a comprehensive characterization of the heterogeneity of cerebellar pathophysiological progresses in schizophrenia, which may help in developing future clinical stratification and targeted intervention strategies.
observations.title: Three Cerebellar Imaging Subtypes in Schizophrenia with Distinct Spatiotemporal Trajectories and Biological Characteristics

metadata.summary: Myocardial infarction (MI) causes cardiomyocyte loss and fibrotic scar formation, disrupting electrical communication and impairing cardiac function. Conductive hydrogels have been studied to reconstruct an electroactive microenvironment for the infarcted myocardium, yet their regenerative effect is limited by the impaired function of surviving cardiomyocytes. Here, we developed a mechanoelectrically active and paintable hydrogel capable of converting cardiac motion into localized electrical stimulation to repair infarcted myocardium. The paintable nature of the hydrogel enables easy application onto irregular epicardial surfaces using a customized brush, while subsequent photocrosslinking allows selective adhesion of the hydrogel to only epicardial surfaces, not to surrounding tissues. Under cyclic loading and in contracting cardiac organoids, the hydrogel generated physiologically relevant electrical potentials, demonstrating efficient deformation-induced charge generation. In a rat MI model, the hydrogel providing electrostimulation alleviated ventricular wall thinning and fibrosis, promoted neovascularization and M2 macrophage polarization, and improved cardiac function. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed upregulation of genes involved in myocardial contraction and energy metabolism. As such, our study offers a minimally invasive and clinically translatable approach for cardiac repair and other tissue applications.

metadata.summary: This study generated a transcriptome-wide resource of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) from two clinical groups: subjects with hyperuricemia (HUA, n=15) and subjects with coronary artery disease together with hyperuricemia (CHD_HUA, n=15). Total RNA was extracted from PBMC and poly(A)+ mRNA was enriched with oligo(dT) magnetic beads. Strand-specific libraries were constructed using dUTP incorporation and UDG second-strand digestion, and paired-end 150 bp sequencing was performed on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Clean reads were aligned to the Homo sapiens reference genome with HISAT2, and transcripts were assembled and quantified with StringTie. Gene-level raw read counts and FPKM values for all 30 samples are provided as processed data, together with the paired-end FASTQ files. The dataset is intended to support investigation of transcriptional differences between hyperuricemia and coronary artery disease with hyperuricemia.

metadata.summary: Obesity-induced metabolic cardiomyopathy features myocardial lipid overload, mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic inflammation, with few targeted therapies. Hyodeoxycholic acid (HDCA), a natural secondary bile acid, plays key roles in metabolic homeostasis, yet its direct cardioprotective effects in obesity-related cardiac injury remain unclear. Here, we investigated HDCA effects on high-fat diet-induced cardiomyopathy using in vivo, lipotoxic cardiomyocyte and 3D cardiac spheroid models. HDCA ameliorated cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophic remodeling and myocardial lipid accumulation. Transcriptomics showed HDCA remodelled cardiac programs governing mitochondrial and lipid metabolism as well as inflammation. Mechanistically, HDCA limited cardiomyocyte lipid uptake via TGR5-dependent suppression of CD36 membrane localization, boosted mitochondrial respiration and ATP production, and reduced oxidative stress. HDCA also bound PIK3CA to inhibit PI3K-AKT-mediated inflammation. In 3D cardiac spheroids, HDCA alleviated lipotoxic injury. Collectively, HDCA protects against obesity-associated cardiomyopathy by coordinating myocardial lipid metabolism, mitochondrial homeostasis and inflammatory signaling, representing a promising candidate for metabolic heart disease.

observations.title: Hyodeoxycholic acid protects against obesity-associated cardiomyopathy by restoring myocardial metabolic homeostasis and suppressing inflammatory remodeling

observations.text: Understanding the genetic changes that drove the evolution of human-specific traits is a central goal in biology. Changes in gene expression are thought to be a major source of phenotypic innovations, but identifying the underlying changes in cis-regulatory elements (CREs) along the human lineage has been difficult: functional data from great apes are scarce and unobtainable for extinct hominins, and pinpointing causal substitutions requires knowing which sequences determine CRE activity. Here, we used AlphaGenome, a sequence-to-function deep-learning model, to predict the cis-regulatory effects of ~17 million single-nucleotide substitutions specific to the human lineage and traced their consequences for gene expression evolution across 305 tissues and cell types. The 71,345 predicted cis-regulatory gains lie mostly outside human accelerated regions and arose either through creation of new CREs or, more often, through co-option of CREs ancestrally accessible in other tissues. They are also enriched for distal enhancers and for target gene functions characteristic of the corresponding tissues, suggesting that they contributed to the evolution of tissue-specific biology in humans. Genes linked to more gains were more likely to be upregulated in humans, and in silico reversion to ancestral alleles traced such upregulations to individual substitutions creating transcription factor binding motifs. Comparison with Neandertal and Denisovan genomes revealed that nearly all gains now fixed in humans predate the split from archaic hominins, yet a few modern-human-specific gains contribute substantially to gene upregulation. Our study provides a genome-wide, tissue-resolved map of cis-regulatory changes and their contribution to gene expression evolution along the human lineage.
observations.title: Reconstructing human gene regulatory evolution using deep learning

metadata.summary: Laminopathies comprise a diverse array of phenotypes that involve multiple organs and are caused by mutations in the LMNA gene, which encodes nuclear envelope protein lamin A (LMNA). Cardiac involvement is a prominent feature and a major cause of mortality and morbidity in laminopathies. LMNA interacts with chromatin through lamin-associated domains (LADs) and regulates gene expression. The role of the LMNA in regulating chromatin structure and gene expression in cardiac myocytes is unknown.  We conditionally deleted the Lmna gene specifically in cardiac myocytes in the mouse, isolated the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes, and characterized genomic structure and function at two levels: first, by identifying and characterizing the genome-wide CTCF binding sites by a CUT&RUN assay; and second, the chromatin conformational changes by HiC.  To determine the role of LMNA in genome organization and gene expression we integrated CTCF binding, LAD, Hi-C data with the gene expression (RNA-seq), and DNA double-stranded breaks (DSBs), determined by END-Seq, in cardiac myocytes.  Compared to wild-type (WT) myocytes, LMNA deficiency increased genomic occupancy of CTCF , predominantly outside of the constitutive LADs (cLADs), and increased gene expression at the CTCF binding sites. Likewise, DSBs were highly enriched at the CTCF binding sites. However, only a small fraction of the chromatin compartments was shifted in the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes. LMNA-deficiency changed the organization of one-third of the topologically-associated domains (TADs). The changes were characterized by the merger of 2 or more TADs (60%), mainly in the non-LAD regions, splitting (30%), and shifting boundaries (10%). Reorganization of TADs, however, did not directly affect gene expression or the prevalence of DSBs. A remarkable effect of the LMNA deficiency was on chromatin loops, as it led to a gain of ~ 600 and a loss of ~1000 loops, whose boundaries were enriched in the CTCF binding sites. The changes affected the transcript level of ~25% of the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes. The gain of the loop was associated with increased gene expression, whereas the loss of the loop had the opposite effect. A multivariate analysis showed that differential CTCF  binding  (largest), loops, and cLADs affected the transcript levels of the DEGs, whereas TADs and chromatin compartments appeared to act in concert with these factors  rather than as independent determinants.  In conclusion, LMNA regulates chromatin structure like TADs its role in  gene expression is mediated mainly through CTCF, cLADs, and loops,. The findings provide insights into the molecular pathogenesis of cardiac involvement in the diverse array of phenotypes in laminopathies.

observations.title: Effects of the Lamin A on Chromatin Structure and Function in Cardiac Myocytes in a Mouse Model of Lamin-Cardiomyopathy

metadata.summary: Truncating variants in desmoplakin (DSP) are a leading cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a severe heart muscle disease characterized by fibrosis and life-threatening arrhythmias. Desmoplakin anchors the junctions that hold heart muscle cells together to the internal cytoskeleton, enabling the heart to withstand the force of each contraction. No targeted therapy exists, and DSP is too large for conventional gene replacement. Here we show, in explanted human hearts and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, that truncating DSP variants reduce desmoplakin RNA and protein, and that the resulting haploinsufficiency renders cardiomyocytes vulnerable to cell–cell adhesion failure under contractile stress, preceded by disruption of the cell membrane. Lowering contractile force with the myosin inhibitor mavacamten prevents this failure. Circumventing the size of DSP, CRISPR-based transcriptional activation of the endogenous gene restores desmoplakin expression and rescues adhesion. Haploinsufficiency is therefore the primary defect in DSP cardiomyopathy, and transcriptional activation offers a therapeutic strategy.

observations.title: Desmoplakin Haploinsufficiency Underlies Cell-Cell Adhesion Failure in DSP Cardiomyopathy and is Rescued by Transcriptional Activation

metadata.summary: Diabetic cardiomyopathy is a clinical condition of ventricular dysfunction, with obesity and insulin resistance as the primary risk factors. Under this condition, the heart accumulates fatty acids and encounters lipotoxicity, which impairs cardiac insulin sensitivity and leads to cardiomyopathy. Angiotensin-(1-9) is a peptide of the counter-regulatory axis of the renin-angiotensin system with cardioprotective effects in myocardial infarction. However, its role in diabetic cardiomyopathy is unknown. To explore the role of angiotensin-(1-9), we first induced lipotoxic stress in the heart by high-fat diet (HFD) feeding in mice. Angiotensin-(1-9) was then administered for four weeks using osmotic mini-pumps. Cardiac function was assessed by, and insulin sensitivity was evaluated in tissues after a bolus of insulin injection. Moreover, lipotoxic stress in vitro was modeled by high glucose medium plus palmitate in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs). We show that angiotensin-(1-9) improves myocardial function and reverts pathological cardiac remodeling in mice. Moreover, angiotensin-(1-9) enhances whole-body glucose tolerance and reduces homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). We next demonstrate that angiotensin-(1-9) increases insulin sensitivity in the heart and skeletal muscle but not in adipose tissue or the liver. Mechanistically, angiotensin-(1-9) does not affect insulin signaling in cardiomyocytes at baseline, while it significantly improves insulin action under lipotoxic stress through AT2 receptor (AT2R) and PKA. These findings demonstrate that angiotensin-(1-9) improves cardiac function under metabolic challenge and promotes insulin signaling in cardiomyocytes under lipotoxicity, which may shed light on the therapeutic exploration against diabetic cardiomyopathy.

metadata.summary: Background: Reactive oxygen species are increased across most pulmonary hypertension (PH) etiologies, resulting in increased reactive lipid dicarbonyls, which form protein adducts and impair mitochondrial function. We hypothesized that reducing reactive lipids would reduce right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) and improve cardiac function by eliminating protein-lipid damage feedback loops. Methods: We used 2-hydroxybenzylamine (2-HOBA) to scavenge reactive lipids in three complimentary mouse models of PH: AKR-high fat diet (HFD, metabolic stress), LNAME-HFD (cardiometabolic syndrome), and pulmonary artery banding (PAB, load stress). Cardiac function was measured by echocardiography and catheterization. RV energy metabolism was determined by oxygraphy. Mass spectrometry analyzed lipids and ceramides; O-link and RNA-Seq evaluated proteomic and gene expression in lungs, RV, and LV. Results: Reducing reactive lipids with 2-HOBA resulted in a ~10% reduction in RVSP, reduced diastolic dysfunction, reduced plasma lipids and ceramides, and normalized RV fatty acid oxidation that was severely impaired in the AKR-HFD and PAB models. Proteomic and RNA changes in the lungs, RV, and LV suggested reduced oxidative damage and inflammatory signaling and altered developmental and actin organization signaling; these changes are plausibly associated with the improved adaptation. Some changes were sex specific, including a 4x higher cardiac fatty acid content in males than females. Conclusions: Reactive lipid scavenging improves cardiac metabolic and diastolic function and pulmonary vascular resistance through restoration of mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative protein damage. The magnitude of hemodynamic improvement combined with substantial diastolic function improvement suggests clinical potential, particularly for PH patients with metabolic comorbidities.

observations.title: Reducing Reactive Lipids Improves Cardiac Metabolic and Diastolic Function in Pulmonary Hypertension Models

observations.text:
BackgroundMotor imagery (MI) brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are increasingly investigated for promoting motor recovery after stroke. However, it remains unclear how BCI control improves through repeated training in stroke patients and whether the timing of MI decoding systematically influences this trajectory.

MethodsTo address this question, we implemented a single-case experimental design involving five chronic stroke patients enrolling in a longitudinal electroencephalography MI-BCI training involving their affected hand. Across 18 sessions conducted over six weeks, the onset of a fixed-duration MI decoding window was randomized to occur 1, 2, or 3 s after cue onset according to an alternating-treatments single-case design. Notably, the BCI combined spectral power and functional connectivity features to classify MI states.

ResultsThe MI classification timing had no significant effect on BCI accuracy, fatigue, or spasticity. BCI accuracy increased across training in four of five patients and was accompanied by patient-specific longitudinal changes in local spectral activity and functional connectivity. These convergent trajectories were consistent with acquisition of BCI control, but were not accompanied by clinically meaningful improvement in motor function.

ConclusionsVarying the onset of the MI decoding window provided no systematic benefit for BCI control. Instead, differences in neurophysiological trajectories across patients indicate that MI decoding parameters need to be personalized and reassessed throughout the training. Overall, these findings inform more individualized and effective BCI settings for neuromotor stroke rehabilitation.

metadata.summary: Background. Rheumatic heart valve disease (RHVD) is the leading cause of acquired valvular disease worldwide, driven by autoimmune responses that sustain chronic inflammation and fibrotic remodeling, predominantly affecting the mitral valve (MV). Although immune dysregulation and transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) signaling are implicated, the molecular mechanisms underlying disease progression and their relationship to clinical severity remain incompletely defined. Methods. We performed a tissue-centric multi-omics study combining histopathology, unbiased proteomics of human MV tissue (n=72), and plasma proteomics from an external cohort (n=445). We associated proteomic signatures with clinical parameters. Cross-species validation involved single-cell RNA sequencing from a murine model of autoimmune valvular carditis. Mechanistic studies used primary human valvular interstitial cells (VICs) and a three-dimensional MV mimetics. Results. RHVD MVs exhibited leaflet thickening, fibrosis, immune cell infiltration, and neovascularization, with T-cell abundance correlating with tissue remodeling. Proteomic profiling identified 1,436 differentially expressed proteins enriched in extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, immune response, hemostasis, and multi-growth factor signaling, including TGF-β and insulin-like growth factor binding protein (IGFBP) pathway. Integrated tissue-plasma analysis revealed shared molecular signatures. The mean transvalvular gradient captured the hemodynamic continuum from mitral regurgitation to stenosis and was associated with coordinated with ECM remodeling, cytoskeletal, immune, and hemostatic pathways. Cross-species integration confirmed convergence on ECM remodeling, immune activation, and TGF-β/IGFBP signaling, predominantly in VIC and myofibroblast populations. Mechanistically, TGF-β induced IGFBP5, IGFBP7, and CCN2 expression in VICs, while their silencing attenuated collagen expression. MV mimetics exposed to pro-fibrotic and inflammatory stimuli recapitulated these findings. Conclusions. TGF-β-centered signaling networks drive the coordinated immune, and fibrotic remodeling that characterizes RHVD. The TGF-β-IGFBP axis emerges as a key mediator of VIC-driven fibrosis and links molecular remodeling to clinical disease progression, highlighting novel therapeutic opportunities.

Gene set enrichment analysis showed suppression of TNF signaling, NF-κB signaling, and cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction pathways.  These data indicate that diacerein pretreatment suppresses leukocyte recruitment and inflammatory priming programs in the ischemic myocardium, and provide a transcriptional basis for its cardioprotective effect.

observations.text:
Cuff-based blood pressure (BP) measurement is a cornerstone of health assessment, yet its mechanism remains unclear and measurement error remains substantial1. On the basis of membrane theory2,3, we propose that external pressure generated by cuff inflation follows a hyperbolic-cosine-shaped axial distribution along the artery, forming a pressure-peak zone (PPZ) beneath the cuff. By combining this external pressure with intra-arterial pressure, we constructed a mathematical model that systematically predicts site-specific vascular motion and hemodynamic changes during BP measurement. In humans, multimodal experiments integrating vascular imaging and synchronized invasive and noninvasive pressure measurements validated the model. The PPZ organizes distinct proximal and distal hemodynamics during cuff pressurization: at DBP, diastolic arterial collapse begins at the PPZ; near SBP, only weak residual blood flow traverses the PPZ and disappears once cuff pressure exceeds SBP. These transitions generated identifiable oscillogram features for DBP and SBP, precisely localized by wavelet scanning. The resulting method showed higher accuracy and lower variability than auscultation and conventional oscillometry and was the only method whose estimates did not differ significantly from invasive BP. This study redefines the hemodynamic basis of cuff-based BP measurement, and its mechanistic framework and accuracy may support clinical application and more reliable therapeutic decision-making.

Structured AbstractO_ST_ABSIntroductionC_ST_ABSBrachial cuff-based noninvasive blood pressure (BP) measurement is among the most important measurements in medicine, yet its underlying mechanism remains unclear. Current oscillometric and auscultatory techniques rely largely on empirical criteria and show substantial errors and variability when compared with invasive BP. A core theoretical basis is therefore needed to link cuff-vessel coupling mechanics to hemodynamic changes and to support a more accurate, mechanism-consistent method for BP estimation.

RationaleTraditional cuff-based BP theories assume vascular compression due to a spatially uniform external force. These theories cannot explain prior observations: tourniquet studies using cuffs similar to BP cuffs showed axial central tissue injury; intratissue pressure measurements and direct measurements of cuff contact pressure all showed curvilinear axial pressure distributions. Because the cuff is intrinsically a membrane structure, we hypothesized that sub-cuff pressure distribution should follow a membrane-theory contact model and a Laplace-type equilibrium. By combining this nonuniform external pressure with intra-arterial pressure, we constructed and validated a mathematical model that systematically predicts vascular motion, hemodynamics, and oscillogram changes during BP measurement.

ResultsThe model predicted that the cuff external pressure follows a hyperbolic-cosine-like axial distribution, forming a pressure-peak zone (PPZ) at the cuff axial center, the site of minimal curvature, with external pressure decreasing toward proximal and distal edges. Sub-cuff pressure-sensor measurements and transvenous tissue-pressure measurements in supine participants verified this pressure-distribution pattern and showed that, once cuff pressure exceeded approximately 30 mmHg, cuff pressure and tissue pressure in the PPZ were nearly identical.

On this mechanistic basis, we established a physically constrained mathematical framework that reproduced vascular motion and hemodynamic changes during inflation and linked vascular dynamics to oscillogram morphology. Angiography, intravascular ultrasound (IVUS), computed tomographic angiography (CTA), and multisite invasive pressure measurements in the human brachial artery showed that the model-predicted motion, hemodynamics, multisite pressure, cross-sectional area, volume, and oscillogram changes agreed with measured results. The arterial PPZ was the primary site determining key state transitions of the sub-cuff vessel and the dominant contributor to hemodynamic and oscillogram changes. When cuff pressure rose above diastolic blood pressure (DBP) during inflation, the PPZ first collapsed during diastole, gradually creating two regions with distinct vascular motion proximal and distal to the PPZ. Near systolic blood pressure (SBP), distal pulsations became markedly delayed and attenuated into distinctive low-amplitude delayed pulsations (small waves). When cuff pressure exceeded SBP, pulsations in the PPZ and distal region disappeared, whereas proximal pulsations persisted. These hemodynamic events mapped onto characteristic oscillogram morphology transitions. Using wavelet scanning analysis, we extracted local oscillatory components as reference features for SBP and DBP.

Auscultation, vascular imaging, and synchronized pressure recordings during the cardiac cycle showed that Korotkoff sounds (KS) occurred during early vascular opening and were related to expansion velocity. Our model further allowed estimation of the area-derived expansion velocity near the distal cuff edge; however, KS-generation thresholds vary across individuals. When cuff pressure is close to SBP, weak blood passage produces expansion velocities below the KS threshold, causing systematic underestimation. In contrast, near DBP, mild post-collapse re-expansion may trigger KS prematurely or with delay, leading to substantial variability. The model also showed that the conventional oscillometric amplitude-coefficient method for estimating SBP and DBP can be analytically derived from our mathematical equations. However, because these parameters are numerous and case-specific, they cannot be practically determined; therefore, the maximum amplitude algorithm (MAA) must rely on empirical ratios relative to the maximum oscillogram amplitude. Consequently, MAA exhibits not only systematic bias but also substantial variability.

On the basis of this mechanism, we developed the novel Morphology-Transition Oscillometry (MTO) method for noninvasive BP measurement. For SBP, MTO showed consistently much higher accuracy and lower dispersion in 175 participants (0.39 {+/-} 6.41 mmHg) than conventional auscultation (KS) (-6.58 {+/-} 10.30 mmHg) and oscillometry based on MAA (-6.79 {+/-} 10.58 mmHg), with no significant difference from invasive pressure. For DBP, the bias was 0.14 {+/-} 6.25 mmHg for MTO, -1.15 {+/-} 7.24 mmHg for KS, and 4.85 {+/-} 9.14 mmHg for MAA.

ConclusionThis membrane-theory-based framework establishes a reliable new theory of cuff-based BP measurement, accurately predicting hemodynamic transitions, vascular motion, and oscillogram morphology, as validated by multimodal in vivo measurements. The MTO method derived from this theory measured arterial BP more accurately than auscultation and traditional oscillometry.
observations.title: Membrane theory with multimodal evidence defines blood pressure measurement

observations.text:
BackgroundAlterations in intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) alpha power and anesthetic dose-adjusted EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) have been associated with both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium (POD) among older surgical patients, yet the neurologic underpinnings of alterations in these anesthetic brain response patterns are unknown.

MethodsWe conducted a single center prospective observational cohort study (ALADDIN), of older adults undergoing non-cardiac/non-cranial surgery, which included preoperative structural and resting state functional MRI, lumbar punctures to obtain CSF, 32 channel intraoperative EEG recordings, and repeated POD assessments. To account for anesthetic dose, frontoparietal EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) was adjusted using our established formula: [intraoperative alpha power]/(2.5 - end-tidal MAC fraction). Multivoxel pattern analysis (MVPA) with follow-up seed-to-voxel analyses identified functional connectivity patterns associated with intraoperative ADA-FP alpha power. Voxel-wise regression analysis with threshold free cluster estimation (TFCE) correction was used to evaluate associations between cortical thickness and ADA-FP alpha power. CSF biomarker values were obtained from NULISA proximity extension assays. Delirium incidence and severity was assessed with the 3-Minute Diagnostic Confusion Assessment Method (3D-CAM). Delirium severity area under the curve (AUC) during hospitalization was defined as the sum of all 3D-CAM delirium severity scores within the postoperative hospitalization period (for up to 7 days after surgery). The Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) was used in cases of non-verbal/intubated patients.

ResultsALADDIN enrolled 215 patients, of whom 168 underwent surgery and had high-quality intraoperative EEG data (44.6% female; mean age 70.9 years). MVPA showed that ADA-FP alpha power was associated with altered functional connectivity within the bilateral frontal poles, left superior frontal gyrus and the right superior parietal lobule (p-FWE < 0.05). Seed-to-voxel analyses revealed that higher ADA-FP alpha power was associated with increased connectivity between DMN MVPA regions and DMN, DAN and salience/ventral attention and decreased connectivity with visual regions. Conversely, right superior parietal lobule connectivity shifted towards greater DMN segregation and increased somatosensory/motor coupling (p-FWE < 0.05). Lower ADA-FP alpha power was also associated with lower cortical thickness in left occipitotemporal and superior parietal cortices (TFCE-corrected p < 0.05). ADA-FP alpha power was also lower among participants with (vs those without) postoperative ward/floor delirium (mean difference, 1.33; 95% CI, 0.22 to 2.44; p=0.019), and ADA-FP alpha power was inversely associated with peak delirium severity (spearmans {rho}=-0.26; 95% CI, -0.40 to -0.11; p <0.001) and delirium severity AUC (spearmans {rho}=-0.28; 95% CI, -0.42 to -0.13; p=<0.001).

DiscussionThese findings suggest a functional and structural neuroanatomic basis for the decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power values seen among some older surgical patients, which may explain the association between decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and increased rates of both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium. More specifically, these findings suggest that altered default mode and dorsal attention network connectivity is linked to decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and raise the possibility that preoperative/baseline functional connectivity alterations within these networks may play a role in delirium risk.
observations.title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients

metadata.summary: Nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 2 (NR4A2) is a widely expressed immediate early gene induced by a host of physiological signals such as growth factors, cytokines, and neurotransmitters. In the adult mammalian heart, including in cardiomyocytes, NR4A2 mRNAs increase more than 60-fold in response to beta-adrenergic stimulation. However, the nature of the transcriptional remodeling induced by NR4A2 in the stressed heart has remained poorly investigated. We show here that NR4A2 activation in mouse cardiomyocytes leads to a rapid remodeling of the cardiac microRNA network. A total of 35 miRNAs were down-regulated, including the muscle-specific miR-133a and miR-499. On the opposite, 65 miRNAs were up-regulated, with a strong representation of miRNAs encoded within the imprinted Dlk1-Dio3 domain. Non-coding RNAs from the Dlk1-Dio3 locus are known for coordinating critical steps of cardiac development such as cardiac lineage commitment, cardiac morphogenesis, and cardiomyocyte proliferation, and for inhibiting mitochondrial function in myocytes. The findings shed light on a novel regulatory mechanism controlling cardiac homeostasis, and establish a framework to investigate further the roles played by NR4A2 in cardiac adaptation or maladaptation to various acute and pathological stress conditions.

metadata.summary: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked fatal disorder caused by dystrophin deficiency, characterized by early-onset, progressive degeneration of skeletal and cardiac muscle. Although microdystrophin (µDys) gene therapies provide functional benefit and partially restore tissue architecture, their impact on disease-associated cellular programs remains unclear. We evaluated proprietary codon-optimized µDys delivered via AAV8 under the MHCK7 promoter and a MyoD enhancer in severe DMD rats with an exon 52 deletion (DMDdel52). Therapy achieved sustained µDys expression with 90-97% of myofibers and cardiomyocytes, with proteins levels ranging from physiological to supra-physiological. Treatment preserved muscle function and extended survival beyond the median lifespan of untreated DMDdel52 rats, maintaining ambulation, climbing, weight gain, and muscle strength. Treatment also preserved cardiac architecture and function while preventing myonecrosis and adverse remodeling, with no detectable toxicity despite high µDys expression. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed that µDys treatment prevented disease-associated inflammatory and fibrotic activation of fibro-adipogenic progenitors, preserved a pro-regenerative interstitial environment and muscle stem cell quiescence while preventing senescence marker expression. These findings indicate that early µDys gene therapy preserves muscle homeostasis, function, and lifespan by preventing disease-associated cellular programs from becoming established within the regenerative niche of DMD rats.

metadata.summary: Truncating variants in desmoplakin (DSP) are a leading cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a severe heart muscle disease characterized by fibrosis and life-threatening arrhythmias. Desmoplakin anchors the junctions that hold heart muscle cells together to the internal cytoskeleton, enabling the heart to withstand the force of each contraction. No targeted therapy exists, and DSP is too large for conventional gene replacement. Here we show, in explanted human hearts and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, that truncating DSP variants reduce desmoplakin RNA and protein, and that the resulting haploinsufficiency renders cardiomyocytes vulnerable to cell–cell adhesion failure under contractile stress, preceded by disruption of the cell membrane. Lowering contractile force with the myosin inhibitor mavacamten prevents this failure. Circumventing the size of DSP, CRISPR-based transcriptional activation of the endogenous gene restores desmoplakin expression and rescues adhesion. Haploinsufficiency is therefore the primary defect in DSP cardiomyopathy, and transcriptional activation offers a therapeutic strategy.

metadata.summary: OCT4, SOX2, KLF4(OSK) has been demonstrated to remodel the epigenetic landscape across various cell types, facilitate cellular dedifferentiation, and play an important role in the process of aging and organ regeneration. Here, we report gene expression profile in OSK-treated neonatal cardiomyocytes. The findings revealed that OSK repressed the expression of contraction-associated genes, including Pln, Casq2, Atp2a2, and Ryr2, and also impeded the expression of rhythm-associated genes, such as Myh6, Tnni3, and Myl2. In addition, OSK treatment was observed to inhibit fatty acid oxidation while simultaneously promoting glycolysis in cardiomyocytes. Taken together, our data provide a differentially expressed genes between OSK and control groups in neonatal cardiomyocytes and demonstrate that the overexpression of OSK in cardiomyocytes resulted in dedifferentiation, including structural, electrophysiological, and metabolic alterations, which rendered them in a more naïve state.

metadata.summary: Muscle LIM Protein (MLP) is a key component of the cardiomyocyte Z disc that is essential for sarcomere integrity and cardiac homeostasis.  Loss of MLP function results in (cardio)myopathy phenotypes in animal models and is associated with inherited cardiomyopathies in humans. Here, we identify MLP as an evolutionarily conserved non-canonical RNA-binding protein and uncover RNA binding as a previously unrecognized mechanism involved in its cytoskeletal association. Using enhanced RNA interactome capture together with complementary biochemical approaches, we demonstrate direct RNA binding by MLP and map two short RNA-binding motifs adjacent to its LIM domains. Disrupting these motifs markedly reduces RNA association, including residues associated with cardiomyopathies. Mechanistically, RNA is required for MLP’s interactions with cytoskeletal proteins, and for the formation of higher-order MLP-containing assemblies. Consistently, RNA-binding-deficient MLP mutants exhibit impaired interactions with cytoskeletal proteins and reduced cytoskeletal retention. Our findings reveal the importance of RNA binding for the formation of MLP assemblies, and support the emerging role of RNA as a co-factor in the organization of macromolecular complexes, with potential relevance to human disease.

observations.title: RNA binding by Muscle LIM Protein is critical for ist cytoskeletal association and impaired by mutation of disease-associated regions
